In 1774 James Cook landed on Niue, a raised coral island east of Tonga, and was driven off by its people. He named it Savage Island.

Niue had been settled by Polynesian voyagers from Samoa and Tonga centuries before. Its people kept outsiders at a distance for decades after Cook, fearing the diseases that ships carried to other islands.

The name Savage Island stayed on European charts long after contact became peaceful. Change came instead through Christian teachers in the 1840s and later through rule by New Zealand.
